claims.text: The alloy is fabricated by casting followed by hot isostatic pressing.
The post-HIP initial alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The post-HIP initial alloy has high toughness.
The initial grain boundaries contain no HCP phase.
Cyclic mechanical loading drives localized grain-boundary complexion transitions.
Cyclic mechanical energy promotes localized elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary complexion transitions promote localized nucleation of an HCP phase.
The localized HCP phase is brittle and lowers local toughness.
The HCP phase creates crack-initiation sites at grain boundaries.
Cyclically loaded specimens will initiate cracks earlier than monotonically loaded specimens.
Early crack initiation under cyclic loading will spatially correlate with grain-boundary HCP precipitates.
Cyclic HCP-phase nucleation and crack initiation will produce characteristic acoustic-emission signals.
Monotonically loaded specimens will retain a single-phase ductile microstructure and fracture later than cyclically loaded specimens.
The alloy can undergo brittle fracture under mechanical loading at room temperature and moderately elevated temperature.
The proposed cyclic complexion-transition mechanism applies to aerospace-like service at temperatures up to 300 °C.
The proposed mechanism may be inactive under purely monotonic loading or outside the stated temperature regime.
Cyclic and monotonic tests on specimens with identical initial microstructures provide the controlled comparison for the hypothesis.
Failure to observe earlier cracking, detectable grain-boundary HCP formation, or distinct mechanical behavior in cyclic specimens would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The alloy is defined as already post-HIP while also being defined as single-phase and free of HCP phase; the cited same-system record states that HIP itself is responsible for HCP-phase appearance. This is an evidence-level inconsistency in the stated baseline.
